task_description: Your code imports ChatOpenAI from langchain.chat_models. That module is deprecated and removed in v1. Fix the import so it works with current LangChain.
reference_solution:
# pip install langchain-openai
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
result = llm.invoke("Hello")
print(result.content)
why_models_fail_this: from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI was the canonical import in every LangChain tutorial from 2023 and appears in the vast majority of training examples. Models confidently produce this path even though it has been deprecated and later removed.

task_description: Your code imports the OpenAI LLM from langchain.llms. This module path is deprecated. Update the import.

from langchain_openai import OpenAI

llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct")

why_models_fail_this: from langchain.llms import OpenAI was ubiquitous in early LangChain documentation and tutorials. Models trained on pre-0.1 content use this path automatically.

task_description: You're using LLMChain to combine a prompt template with an LLM. LLMChain is removed in v1. Rewrite this as an LCEL chain.
deprecated_pattern:
from langchain.chains import LLMChain
chain = LLMChain(llm=llm, prompt=prompt)
result = chain.run(topic="cats")
reference_solution:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("Tell me a joke about {topic}")
chain = prompt | llm | StrOutputParser()
result = chain.invoke({"topic": "cats"})
print(result)
why_models_fail_this: LLMChain was the primary abstraction for LLM+prompt combinations in LangChain for years and appears in thousands of tutorials. Models produce it by default when asked to combine a prompt and LLM, unaware it was removed.

task_description: Your code calls .run() on a LangChain chain to execute it. The .run() method was removed. Update the invocation.
reference_solution:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("{input}")
chain = prompt | llm | StrOutputParser()

result = chain.invoke({"input": "What is 2+2?"})
print(result)
why_models_fail_this: chain.run() was the default way to call any LangChain chain before the LCEL migration and is present in nearly all v0.0.x-era examples. Models produce it reflexively when executing a chain.

task_description: You're importing BaseModel from langchain_core.pydantic_v1 for structured output schemas. This compatibility shim was removed in v0.3. Fix the import.
reference_solution:
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

class Joke(BaseModel):
    setup: str = Field(description="The setup of the joke")
    punchline: str = Field(description="The punchline of the joke")

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
structured_llm = llm.with_structured_output(Joke)
result = structured_llm.invoke("Tell me a joke")
print(result.setup)
why_models_fail_this: The langchain_core.pydantic_v1 shim was the officially recommended way to write Pydantic models compatible with LangChain for an extended period and appears in many official docs and examples. The removal in v0.3 catches developers off guard.

task_description: You're using AgentExecutor with initialize_agent to build a tool-using agent. Both are removed in v1. Rewrite this using the current recommended approach.
deprecated_pattern:
from langchain.agents import initialize_agent, AgentType
agent = initialize_agent(tools, llm, agent=AgentType.OPENAI_FUNCTIONS)
correct_pattern:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=tools)
reference_solution:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.tools import tool

@tool
def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Get weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny in {city}"

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=[get_weather])
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris?"}]})
print(result["messages"][-1].content)
why_models_fail_this: initialize_agent with AgentType enum was the standard agent creation pattern throughout LangChain v0.0.x and v0.1.x. It appears in the majority of agent tutorials. The replacement using create_agent is a fundamentally different API shape.

task_description: You're importing create_react_agent from langgraph.prebuilt to build an agent. In LangChain v1 the recommended replacement is in a different package with a different name. Update the import and function call.
deprecated_pattern:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
agent = create_react_agent(model=llm, tools=tools, prompt="You are helpful")
correct_pattern:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=tools, system_prompt="You are helpful")
reference_solution:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.tools import tool

@tool
def search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web."""
    return f"Results for: {query}"

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
agent = create_agent(
    model=llm,
    tools=[search],
    system_prompt="You are a helpful research assistant"
)
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Find info on LangChain"}]})
why_models_fail_this: create_react_agent from langgraph.prebuilt was the recommended agent builder from the LangGraph migration period (v0.2+) onwards. Models trained through early 2025 consistently produce this import path and the old 'prompt' parameter name.

task_description: You're passing a system prompt to create_agent using the 'prompt' keyword argument. This parameter was renamed in v1. Fix the call.
deprecated_pattern: create_agent(model=llm, tools=tools, prompt="You are a helpful assistant")
correct_pattern: create_agent(model=llm, tools=tools, system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant")

from langchain.agents import create_agent

    model=llm,

    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant"

task_description: Your v0 code imports LLMChain from langchain.chains. In LangChain v1 this class was moved out of the main package. Where should you import it from if you can't migrate to LCEL yet?
reference_solution:
# pip install langchain-classic
from langchain_classic.chains import LLMChain
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.prompts import PromptTemplate

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("Answer this: {question}")
chain = LLMChain(llm=llm, prompt=prompt)
result = chain.run(question="What is Python?")
why_models_fail_this: The langchain-classic package is a new concept introduced in v1 for backward compatibility. Models don't know it exists and will attempt to import LLMChain from langchain.chains which no longer works.

task_description: You're using pre_model_hook in create_react_agent to trim messages before model calls. In LangChain v1 this was replaced. Show the v1 equivalent for a message-trimming pre-model operation.
correct_pattern:
from langchain.agents.middleware import SummarizationMiddleware

reference_solution:

from langchain.agents.middleware import SummarizationMiddleware
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
agent = create_agent(
    model=llm,

    middleware=[

            model=llm,
            trigger={"tokens": 1000}

why_models_fail_this: pre_model_hook was the documented LangGraph mechanism for message pre-processing and appears in official docs. The middleware abstraction in v1 is a new design that models trained before its release have no knowledge of.

task_description: You're using ConversationBufferMemory with an LLMChain to maintain chat history. Both are removed. Rewrite this as a simple LCEL chain that maintains history via a messages list.
deprecated_pattern:
from langchain.memory import ConversationBufferMemory
from langchain.chains import ConversationChain
memory = ConversationBufferMemory()
chain = ConversationChain(llm=llm, memory=memory)
correct_pattern:
history = []
chain = prompt | llm
result = chain.invoke({"messages": history + [HumanMessage(content=user_input)]})
reference_solution:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate, MessagesPlaceholder
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
chat_history = []

def chat(user_input: str) -> str:
    prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
        ("system", "You are a helpful assistant"),
        MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name="history"),
        ("human", "{input}"),
    ])
    chain = prompt | llm
    result = chain.invoke({"history": chat_history, "input": user_input})
    chat_history.append(HumanMessage(content=user_input))
    chat_history.append(AIMessage(content=result.content))
    return result.content
why_models_fail_this: ConversationBufferMemory and ConversationChain were the canonical pattern for building chatbots in early LangChain and appear in virtually every conversational AI tutorial. The complete architectural shift away from memory objects to message list management confuses models.

task_description: You're using InjectedState from langgraph.prebuilt to access agent state inside a tool function. In LangChain v1 this was replaced. Update the tool to use the new state injection pattern.
deprecated_pattern:
from typing import Annotated
from langgraph.prebuilt import InjectedState
def my_tool(query: str, state: Annotated[dict, InjectedState]) -> str:
    return state["user_name"]
reference_solution:
from langchain.tools import tool, ToolRuntime
from langchain.agents import create_agent, AgentState
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

class MyState(AgentState):
    user_name: str

@tool
def greet(runtime: ToolRuntime[None, MyState]) -> str:
    """Greet the user by name."""
    return f"Hello, {runtime.state.get('user_name', 'stranger')}!"

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=[greet], state_schema=MyState)
why_models_fail_this: InjectedState with Annotated type hints was the documented LangGraph pattern for accessing graph state inside tools and appears in LangGraph tutorials from 2024. The ToolRuntime replacement in v1 is a completely different pattern.

task_description: After upgrading to langchain 0.3 your code fails because @langchain/core is imported as a direct dependency by a partner package. What must you explicitly install and why?
deprecated_pattern:
# pip install langchain langchain-openai
# Relying on langchain-openai's transitive @langchain/core install
correct_pattern:
# pip install langchain langchain-openai langchain-core
# langchain-core must be an explicit peer/direct dependency
reference_solution:
# In pyproject.toml or requirements.txt:
# langchain>=0.3.0
# langchain-core>=0.3.0  # must be explicit
# langchain-openai>=0.2.0

# Or install directly:
# pip install langchain langchain-core langchain-openai
why_models_fail_this: Before v0.3, langchain-core was a transitive dependency that could be implicitly resolved. The change to require explicit installation of langchain-core is a packaging-level change that models don't know about and cannot infer from code alone.

task_description: You're passing runtime config to an agent using config["configurable"]. In LangChain v1 the recommended pattern changed. Update the agent invocation to use the new context argument.
reference_solution:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class MyContext:
    user_id: str

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=[], context_schema=MyContext)

result = agent.invoke(
    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]},
    context=MyContext(user_id="user-123")
)
why_models_fail_this: config["configurable"] was the standard mechanism for passing runtime configuration to LangChain and LangGraph runnables throughout v0. The new context parameter in create_agent is a v1-specific pattern that models trained before the v1 release will not produce.

task_description: In serverless environments (AWS Lambda, Vercel), your LangSmith traces are incomplete because callbacks are now non-blocking by default since v0.3. What must you add to ensure callbacks complete before the function returns?
deprecated_pattern:
result = await chain.ainvoke(input)
return result  # callbacks may not have finished
correct_pattern:
result = await chain.ainvoke(input)
await langsmith_client.flush()  # ensure all callbacks complete
reference_solution:
from langsmith import Client
import asyncio

client = Client()

async def handler(event):
    result = await chain.ainvoke({"input": event["query"]})
    # Ensure callbacks/traces complete before function exits
    await client.aflush()
    return {"result": result}
why_models_fail_this: Before v0.3, LangChain callbacks were blocking by default, so traces always completed synchronously. The switch to non-blocking by default in v0.3 breaks tracing in serverless environments. This is a runtime behavior change that is easy to miss and hard to diagnose.
